text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness. To understand your condition better, how long have you had the cough, and have you noticed any blood in your sputum?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculosis. The patient is an 68-year-old male with a six-month history of fever, night sweats, weight loss, cough, and weakness, combined with a recent history of incarceration. These are classic constitutional symptoms of active pulmonary tuberculosis. Given the high suspicion, immediate isolation precautions are recommended while awaiting confirmation.
